text:
Karina M: Hey team — need a tight, field-ready 1‑page "SparkNotes" for enterprise prospects. Core pillars: security controls, SLA guarantees, deploy modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). Will be used in outbound sequences, webinar followups, benchmark landing page, and sales playbooks. Target audience: infra/platform leads + product/ML engineering buyers.

Samir: +1. Do we have the exact SLA language we can put on a one-pager (p99, uptime, response time targets)? Need to be conservative and legally review.

Jess: I can draft. Suggest a two-column layout: left = problem + value prop, right = quick bullets for each deploy mode + security checklist + 3 callouts (SLA, cost wins, integration).

Anil: For benchmarks, recommend a single defensible datapoint: median token cost reduction (cache+batching) and p99 latency for Dedicated under typical 4k token requests. Don't overclaim. Example phrasing: "Up to 3x per-token cost reduction via batching and KV caching" rather than absolute $ numbers.

Olivia: For messaging iteration — we'll need A/B variants: one framed for security/compliance, one framed for ops (latency/cost). I can own the ops copy. Jess you take security-focused wording?

Jess: Yep. I'll draft security copy. Include SOC2, KMS/HSM support, VPC options, and note that Private deployments support on‑prem air‑gapped installs. Avoid saying FedRAMP unless legal confirms.

Samir: Routing: when someone downloads the one-pager or clicks the enterprise CTA from the webinar, marketing needs to tag the lead with "enterprise-sparknotes" and route to AE enterprise queue. Also add a metadata flag for "deploy-interest:private|dedicated|hosted" if they indicate preference.

marketing-bot: Noted: create campaign tag "enterprise-sparknotes" and funnel to /ae-enterprise on lead capture.

Karina M: Callouts we want on the page (short bullets):
- Production-first performance: p99 latency target and predictable throughput via Dedicated pools
- Security & compliance: SOC2, VPC, customer KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs
- Deployment flexibility: Hosted API for fast launch, Dedicated for committed throughput, Private for regulated workloads
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles

Anil: Add a tiny benchmark box: "Representative workload: 4k token LLM chat — Dedicated: p99 < 220ms, median token cost reduced by ~2.7x with batching+cache vs uncached single-request baseline" — flag for review.

Jess: I'll put the benchmark box with a footnote: "Representative workload; results vary by model and prompt. See full benchmark brief for methodology."

Olivia: Distribution plan: 1) Launch post (blog/social) with benchmark highlights + link to SparkNotes; 2) Webinar followup email with one-pager attached; 3) Sales playbook update and one-click asset in Salesforce; 4) Paid social for platform/infra audiences.

Karina M: Timeline: first draft by EOD Wednesday (internal review), legal & security review Thurs, final asset + landing page Friday COB. Is that realistic?

Samir: EOD Wed works. I'll sync with Legal Thurs AM to speed review.

Jess: Drafting now — will upload a PDF mock to the shared drive when first pass is ready. Link will be posted here.

marketing-bot: Reminder scheduled: draft-review reminder set for 2054568000 (thread reminder).

Anil: Small copy ask: for the SLA line use "SLA-backed availability and latency targets for Dedicated customers" rather than exact numbers on the one-pager. Details can be in the linked SLA doc.

Jess: Got it. Will use that wording.

Karina M: Nice — also include 2 quick customer-facing bullets for the sales rep to say on a call: 
1) "We provide a unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—same developer experience, different controls."
2) "We automatically route and fallback to maintain availability under capacity constraints."

Olivia: For creative: ask design for two visuals — a compact deploy-mode matrix and a benchmark micro-chart. I'll ping design after draft.

Samir: Who's owning the landing page copy and CTA?

Karina M: Olivia owns landing page + CTA. Jess owns PDF one-pager. Samir owns routing & tag implementation. Anil will validate benchmark phrasing with infra team. I'll coordinate legal and security review.

Jess: Uploaded first pass mock: https://drive.company/sparknotes/drafts/field-sparknotes-v1.pdf (placeholder link)

Olivia: Great. Once legal thumbs-up, I'll wire the lead form to tag "enterprise-sparknotes" and set inbound routing rules.

Karina M: Final check: keep language short and use bullets. No dense paragraphs. Target reading time = 30s. Let's reconvene here after legal review. Thanks all! :pray:
